title: Operator channel foundation: channel interface, Telegram transport, pairing
description:
Serves facts A10, A11, A14 (bound-user filter at transport level), A18 (interface + fake channel). The channel-neutral core and the only Telegram-aware code in the system.

Deliverables:
- internal/operator package: Channel interface sized to ask/tell (Send, AskDeliver → message ref, Events stream, Resolve/edit-after-outcome), operator config types, global config load/save (~/.tick/operator.json, TK_HOME override for tests, 0600 perms), in-memory fake channel for tests.
- internal/operator/telegram: Bot API client over raw net/http (no new go.mod deps): getMe, sendMessage, editMessageText, editMessageReplyMarkup, answerCallbackQuery, getUpdates long-poll with offset management; bound-user filtering; configurable API base URL so tests run against an httptest fake Bot API server.
- Tracked non-secret mapping .tick/operators.json: operator name (tk whoami) → per-channel public identity (bot username, telegram user_id).
- tk channel command group: setup telegram (pairing flow) + status.
notes: 2026-08-16 18:53 - [human] Human decision (Peter, 2026-08-16): global config dir is ~/.tick with env override TK_HOME — renamed from ~/.ticks/TICKS_HOME after u5o merged; code, tests, tracker texts and wiki updated. In-flight 92u was prompted with the old path text; verify its doc comments at review.
acceptance_criteria:
[A30] go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/... passes, covering the interface contract, config persistence, the Telegram client against a local fake Bot API, and the pairing flow.
[A31] tk channel setup telegram completes pairing against the fake Bot API: writes ~/.tick/operator.json with 0600 perms and offers the .tick/operators.json entry; no token-shaped string appears anywhere under .tick/.
[A32] tk channel status reports each configured channel with its pairing state; with nothing configured it says so and exits 0.
